proposals.spec_says: A read timeout (`Completion::Timeout`) ... MUST NOT fail the drive's other jobs. Submission and draining continue, and after the loop each job whose segments did not all complete is reported `Err` with the timeout message — that job only
proposals.code_does: Completion::Timeout fails every still-Ok job of the drive (landed ones included), fills obj_failed[d], stops submissions to that drive; outstanding reads still drained; other drives unaffected; no incomplete-object pass
proposals.old_text: - Preserve the **drain-all-on-error** invariant of FR-054 per drive: never break early while reads are in flight; retain and report the first error per job while continuing to drain outstanding completions. A read timeout (`Completion::Timeout`) carries only the actor's operation handle, not the job tag, and the actor forgets the timed-out operation; it MUST NOT fail the drive's other jobs. Submission and draining continue, and after the loop each job whose segments did not all complete is reported `Err` with the timeout message — that job only (User Story 11 scenario 4). Completions that indicate a broken channel rather than a failed read — an invalid tag, an unexpected completion kind, a disconnected completion channel — still fail every job of that drive and stop its submissions. *(Sync 2026-11-07, branch `fix/dispatcher-j33-repairs` — code authoritative, commit `408a568d0`, `src/pipeline.rs:1402-1420`, `:1481-1495`. Before it one timeout failed every job of its drive. Known gap, tracked as A-15: the timed-out job's memory-tier slot is then released at once, although the drive may still write into it.)*
proposals.new_text: - Preserve the **drain-all-on-error** invariant of FR-054 per drive: never break early while reads are in flight; retain and report the first error per job while continuing to drain outstanding completions. A read timeout (`Completion::Timeout`) carries only the actor's operation handle, not the job tag, so the job it belongs to cannot be named: it fails **every** job of that drive that has not already failed — including jobs whose reads had already landed — and stops further submissions to that drive; the drive's outstanding reads are still drained, and jobs on other drives are unaffected. Completions that indicate a broken channel rather than a failed read — an invalid tag, an unexpected completion kind, a disconnected completion channel — do the same. *(Sync 2026-11-08, branch `fix/dispatcher-j33-repairs` — code authoritative, `src/pipeline.rs:1398-1411`: commit `709153326` reverted `408a568d0` after review of PR #591 — continuing to submit to a drive after a timeout made a late write into a freed slot more likely and let a hung drive hold `batch_lookup` for about 155 s instead of one read timeout. The 2026-11-07 text ("MUST NOT fail the drive's other jobs") is withdrawn. Known gaps: per-job isolation of a timeout (User Story 11 scenario 4) is tracked as A-18; every failed job's memory-tier slot, the timed-out one included, is released at once although the drive may still write into the timed-out one, tracked as A-15.)*
